title: Emerging Technology Weekly Briefing
description: Quantum and post-quantum cryptography, robotics and autonomy, advanced compute, and space-enabled tech.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 22–27. New: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 26 that Ukraine's Blysk laser, made by Carmine Sky and deployed Nov. 19, shot down a jet-powered Shahed while protecting critical infrastructure. No new post-quantum standard, Army autonomy award, or space award dated Nov. 26–27 was opened. The quantum and space subsections are empty.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: Ukraine's Blysk laser downs a jet-powered Shahed in testing
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 26, citing the Kyiv Independent, that Ukrainian forces shot down a Russian jet-powered Shahed drone with the Blysk laser, a system developed by Carmine Sky and deployed on Nov. 19. Tom's Hardware said Serhii Beskrestnov, a defense-tech adviser to President Zelensky, posted video and described Blysk as being tested in active duty to protect an unnamed critical-infrastructure facility. Tom's Hardware said the source report described persistent cloud cover and fog, which can weaken a laser before it reaches a target, and that lasers are expected to augment kinetic air defense rather than replace it.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: Ukraine restores grounded U.S. Puma drones with an anti-jam radio
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 22 that the United States delivered more than 500 RQ-20A Puma AE drones to Ukraine in 2023 and that the fleet had been grounded by electromagnetic warfare. Tom's Hardware said Ukrainian firm Rise Technologies upgraded the aircraft with its Palych communications system. Citing United24 Media, Tom's Hardware said operators can select a frequency band to avoid jammed channels and that range rises to 31 miles, or 50 kilometers, from a basic range of 10 miles, or 16 kilometers. Tom's Hardware said the same communications system was also installed on DJI and Autel drones and on some attack drones.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: TSMC pauses some shipments under the new advanced-chip rule
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 22, citing Nikkei Asia, that TSMC has paused several shipments to Chinese and non-Chinese chip designers while it reviews compliance with a Bureau of Industry and Security interim final rule. Tom's Hardware said the rule requires foundries and outsourced assembly and test companies to treat a 16-nanometer or 14-nanometer chip as an export-controlled advanced computing chip, and that a design with fewer than 30 billion transistors and no high-bandwidth memory still cannot be assumed to fall outside high-performance computing. Tom's Hardware said designers using a 16-nanometer or newer node must obtain documentation from an approved designer certifying total processing performance or performance density if they want to avoid extra review at the fab.
